title: Kynesin Discovery-to-Protocol Interchange Schema
description: Carries the scientific reasoning behind a validated target and candidate into a trial's population definition and eligibility criteria, with provenance preserved. Version 0.8.0 - revised after hand-population against a real run (Act 3). Separates deletion from consideration-and-rejection, links prerequisites and boundary decisions to the criteria they concern, allows register-carried figures to be cited in contested evidence, and admits prose metrics. VALIDATED: hand-populated with nine criteria, six evidence entries, two boundary decisions and a full companion set from run D. Version 0.9.0 - adds required review_action (own vs verify), orthogonal to review_priority, so a reviewer is told not just how urgent a criterion is but whether to take a position or check one already taken. The org (Salesforce Review_Action__c) and skill template v1.1 had diverged ahead of the schema; 0.9.0 closes that gap. No other properties changed - the Criterion_Domain__c rename brought the org into line with the schema's existing criterion_domain and required no schema change. Version 0.10.0 - derived_from_evidence becomes an array of {evidence_id, relationship} objects instead of a flat string array, so each criterion-to-evidence edge carries its own relationship (derived_from / supports / complicates / contradicts). This is per-edge and distinct from evidence.polarity; without it, ingestion would flatten every citation to derived_from and lose the case where a criterion cites evidence that undermines it. Breaking change to the array shape, acceptable pre-1.0 and pre-publication. Version 0.11.0 - adds the extension mechanism the schema has always lacked. The skill template declares that a programme register MAY extend criterion_domain and evidence_class per therapeutic area, while the schema closed both enums; the two positions coexisted from 0.6.0 and only collided when a second therapeutic area was derived - a rule stated in the template and not enforced in the schema. criterion_domain and evidence_class are now open strings whose core values are carried as examples, and any value outside the core set MUST be declared in a new required top-level enum_extensions block with a scope boundary. Extensions are additive only: re-scoping a core value to mean something else is not permitted. enum_extensions is required even for a payload using only core values, which declares empty arrays - an assertion that the payload extends nothing, not an omission. Enforcement of declared-vs-used consistency is a consumer's job; the schema cannot close-enum-check an open string. Note: the schema's core lists and the template's core lists have themselves drifted and are NOT reconciled here - that is a deliberate decision left to the register authority. Version 0.12.0 - adds maxLength constraints to every string field the Salesforce ingestion maps to a length-bounded column, so a payload that would fail to write (STRING_TOO_LONG) is now caught at validation instead of costing a submission round trip. The caps are per-field, taken from the actual org field lengths, not a uniform limit: e.g. provenance.register_version 50, evidence.evidence_id and criterion_id 10, most short identifiers/labels 255, prose long-text fields 1000-5000. Picklist/enum fields were already constrained and are unchanged. Two mappings remain unconstrainable because the ingestion JSON-serialises a whole object into one column - evidence.metric (-> Metric_Text__c, 1000) and the criteria non-criteria detail (considered_and_rejected / deleted_from_precedent -> Non_Criterion_Detail__c, 5000); a very large object there can still overflow. The Handoff external id is composed as <session_id>:<n> into a 255 column, so session_id is capped at 255 but an extreme value plus the suffix could still exceed it - the ingestion should truncate that composite defensively. No shape change; purely additive validation, so a 0.11.0 payload within the caps is also a valid 0.12.0 payload. v0.14.0 adds one conditional rule: evidence is required whenever any criterion carries a derived_from_evidence edge. A criteria-only payload (no edges) stays legal; an edge-bearing payload with an empty or missing evidence base — the provenance-stripped state a serialization defect once produced by coercion — is unrepresentable. v0.15.0 adds two core criterion_domain values, disease_stage and performance_status, and changes nothing else. Both were found the same way and by different runs: a derivation reached for a domain, found none that fitted, and raised it as core-set feedback rather than coining a local extension. The core set was derived from a single oncology maintenance programme; a second oncology programme filed disease stage and extent under disease_histology because no core value fitted, which is a mis-file the schema could not detect - criterion_domain carries examples, not an enum, so no payload was ever rejected for it. Purely additive: every 0.14.0 payload is a valid 0.15.0 payload, and criteria already ingested under disease_histology are NOT restated - criteria are corrected by re-deriving, never in place.

enum_extensions.description: Values this programme's register declares beyond the core sets. Every non-core value used anywhere in the payload must be declared here with a scope boundary, so a consumer can distinguish an intentional area extension from a typo. A payload using only core values declares empty arrays - that is an assertion, not an omission. From 0.14.0 register identity lives in the top-level register block; the register/register_version keys here are the 0.11-0.13 fallback, and at least one identity source must be present.

scope_boundary.description: What this value covers and, explicitly, what it does not. Required so two programmes cannot hold the same value meaning different things.
What this value covers and, explicitly, what it does not. Required so two programmes cannot hold the same value meaning different things.

provenance.description: Where this payload came from. Every field here answers a question a regulator or auditor will ask.

human_confirmed.description: Did a human review the assembled payload before transmission. Nothing may be written to a system of record with this false.

supersedes.description: session_id of a prior payload this replaces. Supersede with lineage; never update in place.

model_current.description: Is the mechanistic account still standing. Per R003 - a criterion derived from a superseded model looks authoritative and is not.

liabilities.description: Known pharmacological liabilities. Most exclusion criteria trace here.

setting.description: e.g. first-line maintenance, second-line treatment, adjuvant

hypothesis.description: Which patients should benefit, and why.

boundary_decisions.description: Ambiguities that had to be resolved before criteria could be derived. This is where reasoning disappears invisibly - the final protocol reads as if the boundary was always obvious.

decided_by.description: agent_unilateral is a flag, not a value - it means a boundary was set without human input and should be reviewed.

produced_criteria.description: criterion_id values this decision produced or altered.

evidence.description: The evidence base criteria are derived from. Criteria reference these by evidence_id.

evidence_class.description: Core values are listed in examples. A programme register MAY declare additional values for its therapeutic area - the core set was derived from a single oncology maintenance programme and does not generalise. Any value not in the core set MUST appear in enum_extensions.evidence_class. Re-scoping a core value to mean something else is NOT permitted; extensions are additive only.

chain_role.description: Position in the discovery arc. Orthogonal to evidence_class.

polarity.description: not_applicable covers evidence classes that are the wrong lens for this target, which is itself informative.

strength_native.description: Verbatim from the source, e.g. 'ClinGen Definitive'. Never discard the source's own framing.

population_studied.description: Per R005 - which subgroup, which endpoint, which data cut. Composite subgroups are not interchangeable with their components.

caveat.description: Must exist as a field, or caveats hide in whichever column is least structured.

source_completeness.description: Per R004 - registry records omit lab thresholds and prior-therapy exclusions.

criteria.description: Maps 1:1 onto the Trial-Readiness Handoff skill output contract, plus structural links the CSV cannot carry.

criterion_domain.description: Core values are listed in examples. A programme register MAY declare additional values for its therapeutic area - the core set was derived from a single oncology maintenance programme and does not generalise. Any value not in the core set MUST appear in enum_extensions.criterion_domain. Re-scoping a core value to mean something else is NOT permitted; extensions are additive only. disease_stage (v0.15.0) covers stage, disease extent, tumour burden and post-surgical residual disease; disease_histology keeps histological and molecular subtype and is unchanged by the addition - the new value stops absorbing rows that were never histology, it does not re-scope the old one. performance_status (v0.15.0) covers global functional-status instruments used as entry gates - ECOG, Karnofsky, WHO. organ_function keeps organ-specific laboratory and functional measures and is unchanged; a whole-patient functional score is not an organ measure, and filing it under organ_function would be a re-scope.

relationship.description: How this criterion relates to this evidence. Per-edge, and distinct from evidence.polarity which records the evidence's own character. A criterion citing evidence that complicates or contradicts it is the most valuable thing this model expresses; a flat citation list cannot carry it.

derived_from_evidence.description: evidence_id references with the per-edge relationship. THE traceability edge - the reason this schema exists. Not every criterion has one: a criterion resting on convention ('all four precedent trials enrolled stage III-IV') cites precedent rather than a characterised finding. Leave empty in that case rather than manufacturing an evidence entry.

attributable_to.description: Which agent this criterion exists because of, in a combination design.

destination.description: Not every derived finding belongs in the eligibility list.

what.description: The criterion as it appeared in the precedent trial.

deleted_from_precedent.description: For criterion_type=neither where precedent HAD this criterion and it is being removed. An array because a single row may bundle several deletions sharing one derivation (see D011). Silently dropping an exclusion from a named precedent design is indistinguishable from oversight.

replaced_by.description: Per D014 - when unsourceable specifics are deleted but the underlying concern is restated.

origin.description: What each part of this criterion came from. Lets a reviewer trust the register and the cited sources rather than the model. A criterion may be decided by the register, worded from precedent, and carry a model-derived threshold - hence an array. Be honest: hand-classification of real output found that almost every criterion contains some model_derived component (composed wording, a chosen threshold, an assembly judgment). Recording that faithfully is the point; review_priority handles triage.

origin_detail.description: Optional per-component breakdown where the criterion is mixed. Keys are field names; values are origin values.

review_priority.description: How much it matters if this criterion is wrong - NOT whether model-derived content is present. Presence-based priority was tried and abandoned: it marked 9 of 9 hand-classified criteria for review and discriminated nothing. high = a clinical, ethical or regulatory position someone must own. medium = a chosen figure or a verification against source. low = non-contentious, or already flagged by grounded=false.

review_focus.description: One sentence naming what specifically needs a reviewer's judgment or verification. Required whenever origin includes model_derived. A criterion may need both verification and judgment on different components - say both. Example: 'Verify the haematology thresholds against the PAOLA-1 protocol rather than its registry record; judge the tightening of the transfusion window from two weeks to four.'

review_action.description: Orthogonal to review_priority. own = a reviewer must take a position; there is a judgment here nobody has made, or one made in session that needs sign-off. verify = the position is already taken and a reviewer is checking it was implemented correctly, or that a figure matches its source. A criterion implementing a register decision is frequently high priority and verify action: high consequence, position already owned.

what.description: The criterion that was considered and not adopted.

precedent_position.description: What precedent trials did, if anything.

considered_and_rejected.description: For criterion_type=neither where NO precedent had this criterion and adding it was considered and rejected. Distinct from deletion: hand-population showed the two were being forced into one field, which made the field say the opposite of its name.

threshold.description: Optional structured cutoff for criteria that carry a real numeric threshold. Emit it only when the rule genuinely has one - absence is the honest signal, and thresholds are never parsed out of criterion_text prose. operator 'between' requires value_upper, and value_upper is prohibited with any other operator - an upper bound beside a one-sided comparison is not a range.

operator.description: How a measured value compares against value. between is inclusive of both bounds.

unit.description: The unit the value is expressed in, e.g. 'cells/mm3'. Omit for unitless scores.

value_upper.description: Upper bound; required when operator is between.

prerequisites.description: Must complete before the trial can open. Distinct from gaps in individual criteria.

blocks_criterion.description: criterion_id values this prerequisite blocks. Without it a reader must match prose to connect an ungrounded criterion to the study that would close it.

contested_evidence.description: Where the literature genuinely disagrees. Both sides cited like-for-like on subgroup and endpoint.

refs.description: Typed pointers, including decision: references. Register entries carry characterised figures the evidence array may not, and hand-population found evidence_ids unpopulatable for exactly that reason.

resolution.description: How the design handles the disagreement. Not which side is right.

register_status.description: Register amendments are proposals, not changes. A wrong register entry is worse than a missing one.

discrepancies_found.description: Register entries found to be factually wrong, with the primary source that contradicts them.

review_summary.description: Counts for the review surface. Redundant with the criteria array by design - a reviewer sees this before opening anything. The honest proposition is not 'few rows need review' but 'here is exactly what needs looking at, ranked by consequence'.

deletions.description: Count of criterion_type=neither. Hand-classification found deletions cluster at the top of the review queue - what was removed needs more scrutiny than what was included, and no protocol review process works that way today because deletions are currently invisible.

criteria_without_register_coverage.description: criterion_id values carrying no decision: pointer. These are positions the organisation has not yet owned. Surfaced as candidate register entries.

payload_scope.description: Whether criteria[] contains every criterion for this design. complete = all criteria. partial = a subset, e.g. one domain or a review slice. amendment = criteria changed since the payload named in provenance.supersedes. review_summary always describes THIS payload, not the underlying run.

register.description: First-class register identity (0.14.0; formerly overloaded onto enum_extensions.register/register_version, which remain as the fallback for 0.11-0.13 consumers). key names the trial register this derivation was read from; method_register_key names the method register that authorised the reasoning.

key.description: Trial register key, slug@version form, e.g. 'ovarian-parp-hrd@1.2'.

method_register_key.description: Method register key, slug@version form, e.g. 'kynesin-method@1.1'.

attach.description: Directs persistence to attach this handoff's draft records to an EXISTING ResearchStudy instead of creating one. The target must exist and be visible to the ingesting user; if it already has a live (non-superseded) handoff, provenance.supersedes must name that handoff or the payload is rejected. Absent = create mode (a fresh CareProgram and ResearchStudy per handoff, the greenfield default).

research_study_id.description: The Salesforce record id (15 or 18 characters) of the target ResearchStudy in the receiving org.

identifier.description: An identifier is an object, not a string. Namespace, level and status are all required for it to actually resolve.

level.description: Per R002 - joining on 'the Ensembl ID' without checking level produces silent join failures.

aliases.description: Per R001 - required for retrieval recall. Older literature predates current nomenclature.

pointer.description: A typed, resolvable reference. Four pointer types were observed in practice; a string field would lose the type.

locator.description: Section within the source, e.g. FDA label section, protocol clause.

data_cut.description: Which analysis. Interim and final figures differ.

metric.description: Decomposed where possible, prose in `text` otherwise. Effect sizes buried in narrative cannot be compared, but a fabricated decomposition is worse than an honest string.

endpoint.description: PFS, OS, ORR. Per R005 - an ITT figure is not a subgroup figure.

text.description: Verbatim numeric claim where decomposition is not available or not meaningful. Producers emit prose far more often than decomposed figures; requiring decomposition invites invention.
